questiontext.text:
Goal

A returned parcel passes through two desks. Each desk adds a note to the front of its docket. The returns clerk must still identify the original reason beneath both notes.

Read
  • fmt.Errorf. Read the second documentation paragraph. Which method does the returned error gain when the format contains %w? What happens if the %w operand is not an error?
  • errors.Is. Find the paragraph beginning "The tree consists of". Which errors does Is inspect while looking for target?
Coming from Java

The reflex is a new exception class that holds the original as its cause, then getCause() at the top of the stack. Go has no cause field and no exception class to declare.

throw new PackException("pack " + item, e);
...
} catch (PackException e) {
    if (e.getCause() == OUT_OF_STOCK) { ... }
}
Required: %w
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Reread the first sentence of Errorf, then work out what pack must return when pick succeeds.
  • Reread the tree paragraph in Is and count how many errors a plain == against the sentinel would miss.

testcode.text: // rules
stock := map[string]int{"lamp": 2} fmt.Println(pack("rug", stock))
stock := map[string]int{"lamp": 2} fmt.Println(pack("lamp", stock) == nil, outOfStock(ErrOutOfStock))
err := pack("rug", map[string]int{}) fmt.Println(outOfStock(err), err == ErrOutOfStock)
deep := fmt.Errorf("courier: %w", pack("rug", map[string]int{})) fmt.Println(deep) fmt.Println(outOfStock(deep), outOfStock(nil))

expected.text: courier: pack rug: out of stock true false

testcode.text: fmt.Println(outOfStock(fmt.Errorf("crate marked out of stock by mistake")))

name.text: WAT 15.2: Is, As, and the Chain!

questiontext.text:
Goal

A telegram passes through several relay stations. Each operator adds the station name before sending it onwards. Some station names match known fault names, but that does not make them the original fault. The final clerk must identify the real fault.

Read
  • errors.As. Read the first paragraph and those beginning "For most uses" and "An error matches target". What does As do with target after a match? What form must target have?
  • In the example on the same page, what is the type of pathError? What does the call pass as target?
  • errors.Is. Find the paragraph beginning "The tree consists of". Do extra wrapping layers between err and the sentinel change the result from Is?
Coming from Java

The reflex is catch (QuotaException e) for the typed fault and a string check on the message for the sentinel. After two stamps the outermost error comes from fmt, and its message starts with a station name.

} catch (QuotaException e) {
    return e.size - e.limit;
} catch (TelegraphException e) {
    if (e.getMessage().contains("wire closed")) { ... }
}
Banned: ==. Required: errors.As
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Check the type send returns for a quota fault, then reread the sentence in As about what target must point to.
  • For closed, the station name and the fault text share one message string, so reread what counts as a match in Is.

testcode.text: // rules
fmt.Println(relay([]string{"Ashburton"}, 12, 10)) fmt.Println(relay([]string{"Ashburton"}, 3, 0))

expected.text: Ashburton: size 12 exceeds limit 10 Ashburton: wire closed

testcode.text: err := relay(nil, 12, 10) fmt.Println(overBy(err), closed(err)) fmt.Println(overBy(send(3, 0)), closed(send(3, 0)))

err := relay([]string{"Ashburton", "Timaru"}, 12, 10) fmt.Println(err) fmt.Println(overBy(err), closed(err)) down := relay([]string{"Ashburton", "Timaru", "Oamaru"}, 12, 0) fmt.Println(down) fmt.Println(overBy(down), closed(down))

expected.text: Timaru: Ashburton: size 12 exceeds limit 10 2 false Oamaru: Timaru: Ashburton: wire closed 0 true

testcode.text: prank := relay([]string{"wire closed"}, 12, 10) fmt.Println(prank, overBy(prank), closed(prank)) sly := relay([]string{"size 99 exceeds limit 1"}, 2, 0) fmt.Println(sly, overBy(sly), closed(sly)) fmt.Println(relay([]string{"Timaru"}, 3, 10) == nil, overBy(nil), closed(nil))

expected.text: wire closed: size 12 exceeds limit 10 2 false size 99 exceeds limit 1: wire closed 0 true true 0 false

questiontext.text:
Goal

The customs desk marks a form as clean when an inspector reports no problem. One inspector returns an empty envelope that still carries his name. The desk treats that envelope as a finding.

Read
  • Comparison operators. Find the bullet beginning "Interface types that are not type parameters". Which two parts must match for interface values to be equal? When does an interface equal nil?
  • Variables. Read the dynamic-type paragraph and its four-line example. After x = v, what value does x hold? What is x's dynamic type? Does it still hold the original nil?
Coming from Java

The reflex is to return the pointer the helper gave back, because a Java null is null whatever its declared type.

Finding inspect(List<String> form) { ...; return null; }
Exception review(List<String> form) { return inspect(form); } // null stays null
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • The type review returns is not the type inspect returns, so reread the interface bullet in Comparison operators.
  • Check what review returns on the clean path against the x = v line in Variables, then decide whether that value has a dynamic type.

testcode.text: fmt.Println(verdict(review([]string{"name", "", "date"}))) fmt.Println(verdict(review([]string{"a line that runs on"})))
fmt.Println(verdict(review([]string{"name", "date"})))
err := review([]string{"name", "date"}) fmt.Println(err == nil) fmt.Println(verdict(err))
var f *Finding var err error = f fmt.Println(f == nil, err == nil)
fmt.Println(verdict(nil), verdict(review(nil))) fmt.Println(review([]string{"ok", "", "x"}), review([]string{"ok"}) == nil)

questiontext.text:
Goal

A museum program checks whether each visitor qualifies for a concession ticket. An AI-generated version panics when one roster line is smudged, which stops the whole ticket desk. Fix it before the school holidays without breaking the passing cases. Every failure now returns 0 as the age and an error. For the field old the error reads parse age "old": plus the wrapped Atoi error, and for -3 it reads negative age -3. The roster line Bob gives malformed line "Bob", and a visitor Zed with no entry gives no entry for Zed. When the age fails to parse, ageOf puts the visitor's name in front, as Bob: parse age ....

Read
  • Defer, Panic, and Recover. Find the paragraph beginning "Panic is a built-in function". If nothing recovers a panic, where does control go? What happens to the program?
  • Find the paragraph about the json package and the following paragraph. Despite panicking internally, what does the package return to callers?
Coming from Java

The reflex is throw new IllegalArgumentException for any input the method rejects, with a catch somewhere up the stack. The starter code does the same with panic, and nothing up the stack catches the panic.

static int parseAge(String field) {
    int n = Integer.parseInt(field); // throws NumberFormatException
    if (n < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("negative age " + field);
    return n;
}
Banned: panic. Required: %w
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Each panic call names one failure, so hand that failure back in the second return value with 0 beside it.
  • Reread which Errorf verb keeps the error that strconv.Atoi returned inside the error you return.

testcode.text: // rules
age, err := ageOf([]string{"Cy,101", "Di,0"}, "Cy") fmt.Println(age, err == nil)
age, err := ageOf([]string{"Ada,36", "Bob,old"}, "Bob") fmt.Println(age, err) age, err = ageOf([]string{"Di,-3"}, "Di") fmt.Println(age, err)

expected.text: 0 Bob: parse age "old": strconv.Atoi: parsing "old": invalid syntax 0 Di: negative age -3

testcode.text: age, err := ageOf([]string{"Ada,36", "Bob"}, "Zed") fmt.Println(age, err) age, err = ageOf([]string{"Ada,36"}, "Zed") fmt.Println(age, err) age, err = ageOf([]string{"Ada,36", "Bob"}, "Ada") fmt.Println(age, err == nil)

expected.text: 0 malformed line "Bob" 0 no entry for Zed 36 true
